clue.text: Crazy proposal for travel

parts.note: loco is Spanish-derived slang for mad
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: Someone pitches a wild new plan for getting around.
explanation.definitionFit: Locomotion is the act or power of moving from place to place, a synonym for travel as a noun.

clue.text: Pretend to sing along with South Korean rapper in Long Island and North Carolina

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the pair of state and island abbreviations

parts.note: LI is the standard abbreviation for Long Island
Psy is the South Korean rapper behind Gangnam Style
NC is the postal code for North Carolina

explanation.surface: A Korean star mimes to his track at gigs on Long Island and in North Carolina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretend to sing along' looks like one phrase, but 'along with' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: To lip-sync is to move the lips in time with a recording, miming instead of singing.

clue.text: Surprisingly tiny trace leads to conviction

indicators.note: a surprising result is unexpected, so the letters turn up in an unforeseen order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A minute bit of forensic evidence unexpectedly secures a guilty verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom sense of conviction is the false trail; here it means firm belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Conviction in the sense of firmly held belief means being sure, which is certainty.

clue.text: Lists to choose from when a planet's face is magnified by a factor of 200

indicators.text: face is magnified by a factor of 200
indicators.note: the front letter, read as a Roman numeral, is replaced by the numeral worth two hundred times as much

parts.note: Venus is the second planet from the sun

explanation.surface: Restaurant menus are pictured beside a telescope that enlarges a planet's surface.
explanation.walkthrough: V is the Roman five and M the Roman thousand, so swapping V for M multiplies by 200.
explanation.definitionFit: Menus list the dishes on offer so that diners can pick what they want.

clue.text: Academic exercise for Rev. Spooner: style hair with a candle

indicators.note: Rev. Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the starts of two words trade places

parts.note: to perm hair is to set it in waves or curls
a taper is a thin candle
Spooner swaps the opening P and T of the two words

explanation.surface: A quirky academic assignment: give someone a perm by candlelight.
explanation.definitionFit: A term paper is an essay a student writes over a school term, an academic assignment.

clue.text: Robes evidently concealing fat

indicators.note: concealing means the words hold the answer inside them, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Loose robes clearly hide a large figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means very overweight, a synonym for fat as an adjective.

clue.text: Assistant reversing digital divide?

indicators.note: reversing means the phrase that follows is read from its last letter back to its first

parts.note: E- is the prefix for electronic or digital, as in e-mail
a divide between groups is a gap

explanation.surface: A helper somehow undoes the digital divide, the gap between those with and without internet access.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'digital divide' is the wordplay: E-GAP read backwards gives PAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A page is a young attendant or helper, as in a congressional or hotel page.

clue.text: Judge came down against the essence of Roe

parts.note: alit is a past tense of alight, to come down and land

indicators.note: the essence is the heart of something, so only the central letter of the name is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of the three

explanation.surface: A judge ruling against Roe v. Wade, the US abortion-rights case.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Alito is a US Supreme Court justice; 'against' just puts the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Alito sits on the US Supreme Court, so he is an example of a judge.

clue.text: The smallest quantity of soda, unopened, overcoming endless thirst

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming over means being placed above, so one piece sits on top of the other
something unopened has not had its top taken off, read here as losing its first letter

parts.note: Pepsi is a brand of soda

indicators.note: endless means without an end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to long for something is to thirst for it

explanation.surface: A sip of soda, still sealed, beats a raging thirst.
explanation.walkthrough: Soda here is the US word for a fizzy soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics epsilon stands for an arbitrarily small positive quantity, used in limits.

clue.text: Brutally scare the faculty

indicators.note: something treated brutally is violently knocked about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the two words taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to terrify the academic staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is part of the letters to be shuffled, leaving 'faculty' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A school's faculty is its body of instructors, so the faculty means its teaching staff.

clue.text: Business associate sending back money for housing strike

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: rent is what is paid for a place to live
to rap is to strike sharply

explanation.surface: A business associate returns the rent money in the middle of a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner is a co-owner of a business, someone who shares its risks and profits.

clue.text: Yale student invested in plastic dyes — they keep out the light

indicators.note: money invested in something goes inside it, so one piece is placed within another
plastic material can be moulded into any shape, so the letters are remoulded

parts.note: taken as written
Eli is the nickname for a Yale student, after Elihu Yale

explanation.surface: A Yale student puts money into plastic dyes, a business for blocking light.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli, for a Yale student or graduate, is an American crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyelids close over the eyes and so shut out light, a cryptic description rather than a synonym.

clue.text: You sat awkwardly with a poet

indicators.note: something done awkwardly is clumsy and out of order, so the letters get jumbled

parts.note: ye is the old form of you
taken as written

explanation.surface: You sat uncomfortably beside a poet at a reading.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was the Irish poet and Nobel laureate, so he is an example of a poet.

clue.text: Where some children learn arrangement of crop holes

indicators.note: an arrangement sets things in a new order, so these letters are put in a different sequence

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A farm lesson in which children see how holes are laid out for planting crops.
explanation.definitionFit: A preschool is a nursery for children too young for kindergarten, a place where they learn.

clue.text: Think about a swindle, with employee behind schedule

parts.note: a con is a swindle
a temp is a temporary employee
behind schedule means late

explanation.surface: Someone considers a scam involving a staff member who is running late.
explanation.definitionFit: To contemplate is to consider or ponder something at length, a synonym for the phrase.

clue.text: Load in established staple of the slow-food movement?

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the abbreviation that frames it

parts.note: est. is the abbreviation for established, as on shop signs
cargo is a load carried by ship or plane

explanation.surface: A note about loading supplies for a firm promoting unhurried local cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: Slow Food is a real movement against fast food; the question mark flags the joke that snails are the slowest food.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargots are snails cooked as a dish, and snails are proverbially slow, hence the playful definition.

clue.text: Three-digit sequences are not DC poems

parts.note: taken as written
alternating current, AC, is the other kind from direct current, DC
odes are lyric poems

explanation.surface: A claim that Washington DC has no poetry written in numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: DC looks like the capital, but it is direct current; its opposite gives AC.
explanation.definitionFit: North American telephone area codes are three digits long, such as 212 for Manhattan.

clue.text: Miscellaneous source of heat, without liquid

parts.note: the sun is the Earth's great source of heat
something dry has no liquid in it

explanation.surface: An odd assortment: a heater that has run out of fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundry means various or assorted, an adjective that is a close synonym of miscellaneous.

clue.text: Herb interrupts insult to get attention

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a slight is a snub or insult
pot is slang for marijuana, the herb

explanation.surface: A man named Herb breaks in with a rude remark to be noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: Herb looks like a man's name; it is the plant, slang pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the spotlight means being the focus of public notice, so it stands for attention.

clue.text: See 17
Site of the Taj Mahal seen in poorly illuminated illustration

indicators.note: a thing seen in another is set inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: dim means poorly lit
Agra is the Indian city where the Taj Mahal stands

explanation.surface: A dark picture showing where the Taj Mahal stands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Site of the Taj Mahal' wants to be the definition; the answer is the illustration.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a simple drawing that explains something, a kind of illustration.

clue.text: Where you could get milk or grain, in the past, with raw material

parts.note: corn is a grain
erst is an archaic word for formerly
ore is rock mined as raw material for metal

explanation.surface: A question about where you once bought milk or grain and other farm goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Milk or grain' reads as one shopping list, but only milk belongs to the definition; grain starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A corner store is a small neighbourhood shop that sells everyday groceries such as milk.

clue.text: Shred laciest part of some underwear

indicators.note: to shred is to tear into pieces, so the letters are torn apart and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tear up the laciest bit of the lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic is the stretchy band in waistbands and straps of many undergarments.

clue.text: In the far south, tactic ran off the rails

indicators.note: a train that runs off the rails is wrecked, so these letters crash into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A polar expedition's plan went badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran' does double duty in the surface but is part of the letters; only 'off the rails' signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Antarctic describes the region around the South Pole, the furthest south on Earth.

clue.text: Diminutive cover for the state's lawyer, at present

indicators.note: a cover wraps around what it protects, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: toy describes a very small breed, as in toy poodle
a DA, district attorney, is the US prosecutor who represents the state

explanation.surface: A small-time stand-in for the state prosecutor, for now.
explanation.definitionFit: Today can mean nowadays or in the current era, a synonym for at present.

clue.text: Naked star (a well-known doll) is not available

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outside letters are removed

parts.note: the word as printed, which then loses its outer letters
Ken is Barbie's boyfriend, a famous doll

explanation.surface: A star posing nude for a doll line is not free that day.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like an aside about the star but supplies the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat or person that is taken is already spoken for, so not available.

clue.text: Wood from a plank, turned over

indicators.note: a thing turned over is flipped end to end, so the letters come back in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
a slab is a thick flat piece, like a plank

explanation.surface: Carpenters identify the timber by flipping a plank over.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light tropical timber used for models, so it is a kind of wood.

clue.text: Stall an assassin

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small market stand or kiosk
second meaning: John Wilkes ..., who shot Abraham Lincoln

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stall' reads as a verb about delaying an assassin; it is a noun for a market stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A booth is a small enclosed stand at a fair, and Booth was the man who killed President Lincoln.

clue.text: Terribly bored, sanction magazine

indicators.note: something done terribly is botched, so the letters of the next word come out mangled

parts.note: taken as written
to OK something is to sanction or approve it

explanation.surface: Someone utterly bored decides to ban a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Redbook is a long-running American women's magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Redbook is the title of a US monthly periodical, so it is an example of a magazine.

clue.text: Water shortage is severe within the boundaries of Detroit

indicators.note: within places one piece inside the other, framed on both sides
a boundary is an edge, so only the outermost letters of the city name are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the city name
rough treatment is severe treatment

explanation.surface: A severe water shortage has hit the Detroit area.
explanation.definitionFit: A drought is a long spell without rain, which leaves water in short supply.

clue.text: Dressing from April 30?

wordplay.note: the day before May 1 can jokingly be called May 0

explanation.surface: A query about a salad dressing dated the last day of April.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the date as MAY plus the digit zero, which looks like the letter O; the question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is the short name for mayonnaise, a dressing for salads and sandwiches.

clue.text: It might keep you from suffering a retreat before a male jerk

definitions.text: It might keep you from suffering

parts.note: taken as written
a nest is a snug hideaway or retreat
he is the male pronoun
a tic is an involuntary jerk of a muscle

explanation.surface: Advice that a jerky man's rest might spare you pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The American spelling, without the A after the first E, is what the letters build.
explanation.definitionFit: An anesthetic numbs sensation, so a patient is spared pain during surgery.
